name: <creature name (one-line identity)>
_how_to_write: Translate this creature's design claims into measurable claims. Each may carry a label (plain-language description; failure messages quote it). Parts are identified by MATERIAL NAME — the material name IS the part name, naming must match the spec JSON palette (material name = part name).

_claim_types.part_exists: {part} a material/part with this name must exist
_claim_types.part_visible: {part, view?, min_share} minimum share of body pixels the part holds in a given view (view: front/side/tq/reartq/top, default side)
_claim_types.part_signature: {part, view?, min_share, or_min_span} signature part: frame share OR span ratio must clear its bar
_claim_types.style_dark: {view?, max_median_lum} dark styling: cap on body median luminance (0-255)
_claim_types.saturation_area: {view?, min?, max?} share of the view carrying a highly saturated colour (HSV S ≥ 0.50 on the UNLIT baked colour, default view tq, default band 0.10-0.34): under the floor the creature reads as a grey mass, over the ceiling saturation stops working as a spotlight. Says HOW MUCH, never WHERE
_claim_types.anim_named: {names:[...]} these named animations must be present
_claim_types.focal_contrast: {a, b, min_ratio?} the two focal parts' shares must differ by ≥N× (default 2); equal-weight competition is forbidden

claims.label: the signature must be exaggerated: share or span must clear its bar
high-saturation area must sit in the 10%-34% band: amount of colour, not where it goes

_stage: Each claim may declare a stage: LOW/MID/HIGH. judge --stage LOW checks only that stage (plus unstaged claims); with no --stage, everything is checked.
